titulo_es: Direct terms: lo, la, li, le

texto: They replace the direct object (the person or thing on which the action falls): **lo** (it / it masculine singular), **la** (it / the feminine singular), **li** (they / the masculine plural), **le** (they / the feminine plural).
**delante del verbo conjugado**: **Lo conosco** (I know it); **La chiamo** (I call it); **Li invito** (I invite them); **Le ascolto** (I hear them) are usually placed.
**mi** (me), **ti** (te), **ci** (nos), **vi** (os): **Mi conosci?** (do you know me?); **Ti aspetto** (I hope you).

frases.it: Sì, li conosco molto bene! Sono simpatici.
frases.es: Sí, ¡los conozco muy bien! Son simpáticos.
frases.en: Yes, I know them very well! They're nice.

frases.it: Li inviti alla tua festa stasera?
frases.es: ¿Los invitas a tu fiesta esta noche?
frases.en: You're inviting them to your party tonight?
Sure! And you know Chiara too?

frases.it: La conosco poco, ma la chiamo volentieri per invitarla.
frases.es: La conozco poco, pero la llamo con gusto para invitarla.
frases.en: I know her very little, but I'm happy to call her to invite her.

frases.it: Ottimo! Io cerco il suo numero e te lo mando.
frases.es: ¡Estupendo! Yo busco su número y te lo mando.
frases.en: Great! I'll get his number and send it to you.

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «I see them.» referring to a masculine group?

opciones.explicacion: «Li» is the plural direct pronoun masculine and precedes the verb.
«Le» is used for the plural feminine.
«Lo» corresponds to singular masculine («I see it.»).

bloques.pregunta: What is the right way for «I know him.»?

opciones.explicacion: The «lo» pronoun previews the «conosco» verbal form.
In Italian the tone pronouns are not postponed to the conjugated verb.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the pronoun for Paolo (masculine singular).

opciones.explicacion: Paolo is masculine singular, so the right pronoun is «lo».
It refers to a feminine singular noun.
It refers to a plural masculine.

bloques.pregunta: What does the talking person say?
bloques.frase: La conosco molto bene perché lavoriamo insieme.

opciones.texto: He knows a woman very well because they work together.
opciones.explicacion: «La» refers to a direct object feminine singular.

opciones.texto: He knows a number of co-workers very well.
opciones.explicacion: It would be «li conosco» or «le conosco» in plural.

opciones.texto: He doesn't know anyone in his new office.
opciones.explicacion: He clearly states that he knows her very well.

bloques.pregunta: What action does the phrase describe?
bloques.frase: Li invito alla festa di compleanno stasera.

opciones.texto: I invite my friends to the birthday party tonight.
opciones.explicacion: «Li invito» expresses the invitation to a masculine or mixed group.

opciones.texto: Friends invite me to their party tonight.
I can't go to the party with my friends.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase confirms the active invitation to them.

bloques.frase: Lo conosco bene da tanto tempo
bloques.traduccion: I've known him a long time.
bloques.explicacion: Right placement of the direct pronoun atone to the verb.

bloques.pregunta: What is the right answer to «Conosci Chiara?»?

opciones.explicacion: «Chiara» is feminine singular: it is replaced by «la».

intro: In order not to repeat again and again the name of a person or thing, the Italian uses the direct pronouns: «lo», «la», «li», «le».
